behavior_constraints: CLI binary repro-verify supports subcommands verify-checkpoint, compare-outputs, validate-manifest, audit-lineage, generate-report, and merge-checkpoints.

verify-checkpoint parses MLCK binary with 16-byte header magic MLCK, version uint32 LE == 1, tensor count, metadata length, UTF-8 JSON metadata, repeated tensor records, and a 32-byte SHA-256 footer over all preceding bytes.
Dtype mapping is 0=float32 size4, 1=float64 size8, 2=int32 size4, 3=int64 size8; tensor data length must equal product(shape)*sizeof(dtype).

verify-checkpoint outputs JSON with valid, format_version, num_tensors, metadata, tensor name/dtype/shape/checksum, and file_checksum; invalid files output {valid:false,error:...}, exit 1; valid files exit 0.
Checkpoint validation fails on bad magic, unsupported version, checksum mismatch, truncation, malformed metadata, or inconsistent tensor data size.
compare-outputs requires two valid MLCK files, matches tensors by name, and supports --atol default 1e-7, --rtol default 1e-5, --mode strict|relaxed.
Comparison mismatch occurs when |a-b| > atol + rtol*|b|; strict requires zero mismatches; relaxed allows up to 0.1% outliers per tensor.

compare-outputs outputs JSON with match, mode, atol, rtol, tensor_results, missing_in_file1, missing_in_file2; overall match is true only when all tensors match and no tensors are missing in either file; exit 0 for match, 1 otherwise.

validate-manifest parses TOML and requires experiment.name non-empty, experiment.timestamp RFC3339, environment.python_version semver-like 3.x.y, environment.seed integer >=0, environment.deterministic boolean, dependencies array of tables with name and version strings, outputs.checkpoint_path non-empty, and outputs.metrics table with at least one numeric field.
validate-manifest emits warnings for missing optional environment.gpu_id, environment.cuda_version, git.commit, and git.branch; outputs valid with warnings or errors; exit 0 if valid, 1 if invalid.
entities.summary: This round demands a new Go CLI, repro-verify, implementing MLCK checkpoint verification, comparison, manifest validation, lineage DAG auditing, report generation, and checkpoint merging with JSON outputs and exit codes.

instruction_head:
Build a command-line tool called `repro-verify` in Go that verifies the integrity and reproducibility of machine learning model checkpoints and experiment artifacts.

The tool must support these subcommands:

## `repro-verify verify-checkpoint <file>`

behavior_constraints: Root-level dotted TOML keys such as experiment.name = "test" without an [experiment] header resolve into nested fields instead of disappearing.
Inline TOML comments after values are stripped and do not become part of parsed values.
Existing valid manifest validation and all existing correct command outputs remain identical.
verify-checkpoint invalid checkpoint JSON and validate-manifest invalid manifest JSON payloads remain unchanged.
Usage errors, unreadable inputs, invalid arguments, and error paths for compare-outputs, merge-checkpoints, and drift-analysis output {"error":"<message>"} on stdout and exit code 1.
Top-level no-argument and unknown-subcommand cases output {"error":"<message>"} on stdout and exit code 1.
verify-checkpoint and validate-manifest non-content usage/unreadable errors use the generic {"error":"<message>"} shape while invalid-content payloads stay unchanged.
No specified error path emits only plain text to stderr.

entities.summary: This round fixes root-level dotted TOML key and inline comment parsing and standardizes CLI error reporting to JSON error objects on stdout while preserving existing command-specific failure payloads and correct outputs.

instruction_head:
The TOML parsing is fragile. Dotted keys at root level (`experiment.name = "test"` without a `[experiment]` header) don't resolve — the field just vanishes. Inline comments after values (`name = "test" # comment`) bleed into the parsed value. Fix both.
